explanation: L1/N400+ is a concrete-attribute detector: it fires on the word (or word-piece) that names a perceptible property or a physical part of a concrete thing - colour terms (green, gray, brown, blue, black), side/position terms (side, centre, corner, bottom), measure and unit terms (hours, minutes, degrees, teaspoon, cup), and physical component nouns that a concrete modifier has just named by material, kind or function ('oak table' 0.9 vs 'the table' 0.1, 'heating elements' 1.0 vs 'the elements' 0.35) - literally or figuratively, plus a few directional particles and ordering adverbs that advance a clause ('out', 'off', 'then', 'before'). It is silent across the closed class (0 of 8706 determiners, and in the scan 'and' 0/2281, 'to' 0/1944, 'is' 0/876, 'for' 0/738) and on relational/analytic vocabulary: 'idea' 0/13, 'company' 0/34, 'work' 0/97 and 'people' 0/77 never fire, and 'main idea', 'new plan', 'central argument', 'founding principles' and 'the elements of a strategy' all measure 0.0, so analytic or technical prose stays below the line even when it mentions concrete objects ('the dimensions of the room were recorded' 0.16).
